channel.title: Typography Gems
channel.description: Free typography watch: typefaces, foundries and tools.

item.title: Lilex 2.630
item.description: A coding font derived from IBM Plex Mono, with ligatures and a variable version. 2.630 (Oct 5) adds ASCII control pictures, an overline, rounded commas and quotes (ss05), and fixes ligature and diacritic alignment. OFL 1.1, active since 2019.

item.title: Sarasa Gothic 1.0.42
item.description: A composite font combining Inter, Iosevka and Source Han Sans: Latin plus Chinese, Japanese and Korean that line up, including monospaced variants for terminals and code. Version 1.0.42 (Sep 26), as TTF, TTC or SuperTTC. OFL 1.1, mature and widely used.

item.title: Noto Emoji — Unicode 18
item.description: Google's open emoji library moves to Unicode 18 (Sep 24): 2D color font v2.057, a 3D edition v3.054 shipped separately, plus the source SVGs and PNGs. A variable monochrome version is also on Google Fonts. Fonts under OFL 1.1, tools under Apache 2.0.

item.title: HarfBuzz 14.6.0
item.description: The text-shaping engine behind Chrome, Firefox, Android and LibreOffice. 14.6.0 (Oct 5) fixes a regression with out-of-range glyph IDs, and adds the DMAP table and FeatureVariations 1.1 lookup variations. "Old MIT" license, an industry reference.

item.title: glyphsLib 6.16
item.description: The Python bridge that converts .glyphs sources to UFO and designspace, so you can build with fontmake without opening Glyphs. 6.16 (Oct 8) places corner components like Glyphs 3.5, and 6.16.1 (Oct 16) refines instances and alignment zones. Apache 2.0, mature.

item.title: Google Sans Flex 5.000
item.description: Google's brand typeface, released as open source: a geometric variable sans on five axes (weight 1–1000, width 25–151, slant, ROND roundness, optical sizes 1–144). 5.000 (Oct 9) drops the GRAD axis and refines tiny sizes. OFL 1.1, merged into the google/fonts repo.

item.title: Tiny5 and Tiny5 Duo 2.007 — pixel type goes variable
item.description: A 5-pixel-tall pixel font, now variable: weight, width, roundness and two rare axes, BLED (ink spread, CRT glow) and JITT (jitter), plus italics. Tiny5 Duo uses 2-pixel stems. Great for HUDs and retro interfaces. OFL, merged into google/fonts on Oct 9.

item.title: Firjar — a bilingual Kufic Arabic-Latin typeface
item.description: A Kufic-inspired sans built like a compass drawing (quarter circles and clean straight lines), pairing Arabic and Latin in one variable family: weight 100–800, width 75–125. For headlines, branding and bilingual UI. By Mestara Type, OFL, added to google/fonts on Oct 15.

item.title: Fontspector 1.9
item.description: Fontbakery's successor, rewritten in Rust: font quality checks from the command line, as a Python module or right in the browser (WASM), with Google Fonts, OpenType and universal profiles. 1.9 (Oct 9) can fix some issues directly in UFO sources. Apache 2.0.

item.title: LXGW WenKai 1.530
item.description: A free Chinese kai-style font derived from Fontworks' Klee One, popular for reading. 1.530 (Oct 17) adds 50 Unicode 18 small seal script characters, mahjong and dice symbols, completes JIS X 0213 kanji and redraws hundreds of glyphs. OFL 1.1.

item.title: Cal Sans 2.011
item.description: Cal.com's geometric sans, now a variable system: weight 400–700, optical sizes 8–45 pt, a GEOM axis (from A11y to Geo), real italics. 2.011 (Oct 15) adds Cal Sans Phlex, morphing letterforms without avar2. OFL 1.1; Flex is still experimental.

item.title: Kode Mono 2.003
item.description: A coding monospace with ligatures and Powerline glyphs. The 2.0 series adds two variable axes, width (75–125) and roundness (ROND 0–100), plus an ss01 set that tells D/0/O and 8/B apart. 2.003 (Oct 8) is heading to Google Fonts. OFL 1.1, mature since 2023.

item.title: Wavefont and Linefont — charts written as text
item.description: Two variable fonts by Dmitry Iv.: each character becomes a bar (Wavefont: waveforms, histograms) or a curve point (Linefont: time series). Great for tiny charts in a web UI without canvas. Updated on Google Fonts on Oct 9. OFL 1.1.

item.title: Libron 0.31
item.description: A reading serif derived from Readerly (itself based on Newsreader), hand-edited in FontForge for a calmer texture. Ready-made builds for Kobo, KOReader, Kindle, desktop and web. 0.31 (Oct 9) adds fractions, superscripts and Unicode spaces. OFL, in active development.

item.title: Ark Pixel Font 2026.10.16
item.description: An open source pixel font in 10 and 12 px, covering Latin and Chinese/Japanese/Korean, in monospaced or proportional versions with kerning. Perfect for a game UI or a retro HUD. Released Oct 16 (16 px dropped). Fonts OFL 1.1, code MIT, active since 2021.

item.title: Redaction — the legal-document serif, coming to Google Fonts
item.description: Serif by Jeremy Mickel (MCKL), between Times and Century Schoolbook, in 7 families: one clean and six increasingly "photocopied" (10 to 100). Great for textured titles or an archival look. OFL 1.1, Google Fonts onboarding under way (Oct 2026).

item.title: Fontra Pak 2026.10
item.description: The free font editor that runs in your browser, bundled for macOS, Windows and Linux. 2026.10 (Oct 5) adds a proper File menu and a button to open a .ufo or .fontra project directly. GPL 3.0, still in active development, monthly releases.

item.title: Glyphr Studio 2.10.6
item.description: A 100% web-based font editor, no install or account, built for beginners: draw a display alphabet or an icon font in one evening. 2.10.6 (Oct 2, 2026) fixes tool states and search within a Unicode range. GPL 3.0, free.

item.title: Iosevka 34.9
item.description: A narrow, fully configurable monospace (glyph variants, custom builds), available as Term, Slab, Aile and Etoile. 34.9 (Sept 26, 2026) adds variants for ζ, ξ, ς and dozens of diacritics. OFL 1.1, a very mature project since 2015.

item.title: IBM Plex Mono variable
item.description: Plex Mono is finally a variable font: one file, weight axis from 100 to 700, Thin to Bold instances. Handy for code and web UI without juggling files. Joins Plex Serif and Sans variable. OFL 1.1, a very mature IBM family.

item.title: fontc 1.0 — Google's font compiler in Rust
item.description: Stable release (Sept 1, 2026) of Google Fonts' Rust compiler, a drop-in replacement for fontmake for Glyphs or UFO sources: variable fonts compiled much faster. TrueType only, no static instances. Apache 2.0, tested on ~3,450 targets.

item.title: fontTools 4.67
item.description: The Python Swiss Army knife for fonts (ttx, subset, varLib) at 4.67 (Oct 14, 2026): instancing of COLRv1 variable fonts, feaLib and CFF2 fixes. For slimming a web font, freezing an axis or scripting a pipeline. MIT, very mature.

item.title: Geist 1.8.1
item.description: Vercel's Geist Sans and Geist Mono, understated, for UI and code. 1.8.1 (Oct 16, 2026) aligns binary versions with the package and fixes the lowercase omega, which pointed to the Ohm sign. OFL 1.1, regular releases since 2023.

item.title: Monaspace 1.4
item.description: GitHub Next's monospace superfamily (Neon, Argon, Xenon, Radon, Krypton) with “texture healing” that balances wide and narrow letters. 1.400 adds Cyrillic, Greek, Vietnamese and IPA. Variable, web and Nerd Fonts. OFL 1.1.

item.title: Maple Mono 7.9
item.description: Rounded monospace for IDEs and terminals: ligatures, Nerd Font icons, a script to freeze your variants (a “Normal” option close to JetBrains Mono). 7.9 adds IPA glyphs and fixes feature freezing. OFL 1.1, ~29,000 stars.

item.title: Fontsource
item.description: Thousands of free fonts as npm packages to self-host: one import and the font, static or variable, is served by your own site, with no third-party CDN. Online catalog for testing. MIT code, each font keeps its own licence (often OFL).

item.title: Collletttivo — Italian libre foundry
item.description: Italian collective whose whole catalog is under the SIL OFL: Apfel Grotezk, Ronzino, Sprat (18 weights + variable), Halibut, Necto Mono… Expressive display faces usable commercially and in renders, with credit requested.

item.title: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next
item.description: 2024 version of the Braille Institute's hyperlegible typeface: new glyphs, revised kerning, 6 weights with italics (versus 2). OFL 1.1, sources on GitHub, on Google Fonts. Ideal for UI, subtitles and docs.

item.title: Inter 4.1
item.description: The reference screen sans-serif (OFL 1.1), variable with an optical size axis and many OpenType features (tabular figures, alternates). A mature project; latest version 4.1 (Nov 2024). A safe choice for interfaces and pairing.

item.title: FontForge 20251009
item.description: Free and open source font editor (Windows, macOS, Linux), scriptable in Python: draw, retouch and convert your own fonts. A mature project; latest version released Oct 9, 2025. Free (donations).
